title: Organic Reactions Adventure: Polymers and Ethanol Routes
welcome_lead: Today you'll draw repeat units, meet condensation polymers and pick an ethanol route.
meta_desc: GCSE Chemistry stretch — repeat units, addition vs condensation polymerisation, and fermentation vs hydration of ethene.
final_note: You learned to spot repeat units, the difference between addition and condensation polymers, and the trade-offs of two ethanol routes.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Take the monomer, open the C=C, redraw as a single bond and put square brackets around it with n outside.

Ethene CH2=CH2 → −[CH2−CH2]−n which is poly(ethene). Propene gives −[CH(CH3)−CH2]−n which is poly(propene).

Some monomers have two functional groups (e.g. a diol and a dicarboxylic acid).

Each link forms an ester bond and releases water. With n monomer pairs you make a polyester and (n − 1) water molecules. That's a condensation polymer — addition polymers release nothing.

Fermentation: sugar + yeast, batch process, renewable sugar, low tech, low cost — but slow, dilute product, only ~15% ethanol.

Hydration of ethene: ethene + steam over a catalyst, continuous, fast, high purity — but ethene comes from non-renewable crude oil and needs high temperature and pressure.
